The EA79A1004 is an automatic air vent from Resideo (Honeywell Home), industrial duty, 3/4 in connection.

An automatic air vent does one job without being asked: it sits at a high point, and when air collects under it a float drops and lets the air out, then rises and reseals as water returns. It is what replaces walking the building with a bleed key every autumn.

Height is everything. A vent below the highest point of the loop vents nothing, because the air is not where the vent is. Put it at the actual top — the crown of the main, the top of the riser, the high side of the air separator.

Industrial duty here means the higher ratings, and the tapped connection lets it sit directly on a main rather than needing a purpose-built tapping.

Rated to 250 F maximum and 150 psi.

  • Manufacturer Part #: EA79A1004
  • Type: Automatic air vent

  • Connection size: 3/4 in
  • Maximum temperature: 250 F
  • Maximum pressure: 150 psi
  • Dimensions: 5 in long x 1 7/8 in diameter
  • Category: Air Vents

The NK300S-100 is a combination boiler feed valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 1/2 in, sweat and threaded connections.

Filling a boiler needs four things in the same line: a shutoff, a backflow preventer so system water can never reach the potable supply, a pressure reducing valve so the fill stops at system pressure instead of at street pressure, and a strainer. A combination valve is all of it in one body, which is fewer joints to make and fewer joints to leak.

The backflow preventer is the part that is not optional. Boiler water is treated water sitting against steel; the code separation between it and the drinking supply is the whole reason this assembly exists in this form.

Fast fill means it can be opened wide to charge a dry system quickly and then returned to regulating, instead of taking an afternoon to fill through a reducing valve at its setpoint.

What is in the body: boiler fill shut off valve, double check backflow preventer with air vent and discharge connection, valve cartridge, integrated 200 micron strainer, a check valve, pressure reducing valve with valve insert, adjustment spring, and pressure gauge.

The PA404A1025 is a Pressuretrol pressure controller from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 3 psi to 15 psi, subtractive differential.

On a steam boiler the pressure control is what decides when the burner stops. Steam heating works at a couple of psi; a boiler allowed to climb past that wastes fuel, bangs the mains and shortens the life of everything downstream of it. The Pressuretrol senses boiler pressure on a stainless diaphragm and breaks the burner circuit at the cut-out setting.

Subtractive differential. The cut-in is the setting, and the burner comes back on at the setting minus the differential. Set the main scale and the differential subtracts from it downward.

Getting this backwards is the classic mis-set: the same numbers on the two versions do not produce the same cycle. Check which one is on the boiler before copying settings from the old control.

This is an operating control, not a safety limit. A steam boiler still needs its own high-pressure limit and its relief valve; the Pressuretrol is what keeps it from getting there.

The PV-001RP is a replacement vent top for the SuperVent air eliminator from Resideo (Honeywell Home).

The vent top is the part that wears. The float and its seat spend their life wet, and when they finally stop sealing the symptom is a separator that weeps or one that stops venting — not a failure of the body, which is bronze and outlives several tops.

Replacing the top means the body stays in the pipe. No cutting, no re-soldering, no draining beyond what it takes to get to the vent.

Universal fit across the SuperVent range, so it is the same part whatever size body is in the loop.

The PV075 is a SuperVent air eliminator from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 3/4 in female npt connection, 13 Cv.

Why air has to come out of a hydronic loop. Fresh fill water carries dissolved air, and heating it drives that air out of solution. What it does next is all bad: it collects at high points and blocks flow, it gasses through the circulator as noise, it puts oxygen against steel where there was none, and it turns a radiator into a cold half-radiator. A system that has to be bled every autumn is a system that is still taking air in somewhere.

An air eliminator works by slowing the water down. Inside the body the flow spreads out and loses velocity, the bubbles stop being carried along, they rise into the vent chamber, and a float valve lets them out. It runs continuously, with nothing to set and nothing to press.

Flow capacity is 13 Cv. Size the separator to the pipe it sits in, not to the boiler — an undersized body throttles the loop, and an oversized one is money spent on brass.

Threaded NPT connects to anything and comes apart again, which matters on a component that may be serviced.

Put it where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest — on the supply, close to the boiler outlet. That is where air comes out of solution most readily, and catching it there keeps it from reaching the rest of the system at all.

Body is bronze, rated to 240 F maximum and 125 psi.

An air eliminator works by slowing the water down. Inside the body the flow spreads out and loses velocity, the bubbles stop being carried along, they rise into the vent chamber, and a float valve lets them out. It runs continuously, with nothing to set and nothing to press.

Flow capacity is 50 Cv. Size the separator to the pipe it sits in, not to the boiler — an undersized body throttles the loop, and an oversized one is money spent on brass.

Press fittings are made cold, with a tool rather than a torch — which is what gets the job done in a finished basement or anywhere a hot work permit is the long pole.

Put it where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest — on the supply, close to the boiler outlet. That is where air comes out of solution most readily, and catching it there keeps it from reaching the rest of the system at all.
